facts.statement: Zhenyuanlong is known from only one fossil specimen of the species Zhenyuanlong suni.
facts.quote: It is known from a single specimen belonging to the species Zhenyuanlong suni

facts.statement: The single known specimen preserves a nearly complete skeleton with long tail feathers and large wings.
facts.quote: This type specimen preserved a nearly complete skeleton that contains traces of feathers, including long tail feathers and large wings.

facts.statement: Zhenyuanlong lived approximately 125 million years ago during the Aptian age of the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: It lived during the Aptian age of the early Cretaceous period, approximately 125 million years ago.

facts.statement: The fossil was discovered by a local farmer near Sihedang in Jianchang, Liaoning Province.
facts.quote: The specimen was found by a local farmer near Sihedang in Jianchang, Liaoning Province

facts.statement: Zhenyuanlong suni was named and described in 2015 by Lü Junchang and Stephen Brusatte.
facts.quote: In 2015, the type species Zhenyuanlong suni was named and described by paleontologists Lü Junchang of the Chinese Academy of Geological Sciences in Beijing and Stephen Brusatte of the University of Edinburgh in the United Kingdom.

facts.statement: The genus name Zhenyuanlong honors Zhenyuan Sun and means "dragon" in Chinese.
facts.quote: The generic name combines Zhenyuan Sun's given name with the Chinese Pinyin long, meaning "dragon".

facts.statement: The holotype specimen JPM-0008 was found in the Sihedang locality within the Yixian Formation of northeastern China.
facts.quote: The holotype, JPM-0008, was found in the Sihedang locality of Jianchang County of northeastern China's Yixian Formation

facts.statement: The holotype is a sub-adult skeleton that is nearly complete but lacks the rear half of the tail.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen is represented by its sub-adult status, its nearly complete and articulated skeleton lacking only half of the tail

facts.statement: Zhenyuanlong suni was a mid-sized dromaeosaurid similar in size to Tianyuraptor.
facts.quote: Zhenyuanlong suni was a mid-sized dromaeosaurid comparable in length to the similar Tianyuraptor.

facts.statement: The preserved skeleton measures 122.6 cm in length because the rear half of the tail is missing.
facts.quote: The fossil skeleton is nearly complete but lacks the last half of the tail, giving the specimen a preserved length of 122.6 cm.

facts.statement: Including long tail feathers, the animal may have reached a total length of 2 meters in life.
facts.quote: With the added length of long tail feathers, the animal was perhaps up to 2 m in life.

facts.statement: Zhenyuanlong's arms possess unique features rarely seen in related dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Its arms also exhibit some unique and unusual features seen in few related dinosaurs.

facts.statement: The radius of Zhenyuanlong's forearm is among the thinnest of any theropod, comparable only to basal coelurosaurs and alvarezsauroids.
facts.quote: The radius of Zhenyuanlongs forearm is among the proportionally thinnest of any theropod dinosaur, comparable only to a handful of basal coelurosaurs and to alvarezsauroids, which had extremely reduced arms and hands.

facts.statement: Zhenyuanlong is unique among Liaoning dromaeosaurids for having a second metacarpal shorter than the first metacarpal and the first finger bone combined.
facts.quote: Zhenyuanlong is also unique among Liaoning dromaeosaurids for its second metacarpal being shorter than the combined lengths of the first metacarpal and first bone of the innermost finger.

facts.statement: Body feathers are preserved as small imprints on the front and back of the neck.
facts.quote: The body feathers of Zhenyuanlong are represented by small regions of imprints in the front and back of the neck.

facts.statement: The wing feathers were very long, exceeding twice the length of the upper arm bone.
facts.quote: Despite its small arms, the feathers that made up the wings were very long, more than twice the length of the humerus (upper arm).

facts.statement: Each wing had a broad surface area of approximately one square meter.
facts.quote: The wings were broad, with a total surface area of about one square meter each

facts.statement: The wing coverts are preserved as a row of about 30 small feathers attaching perpendicularly to the ulna and third metacarpal.
facts.quote: These are preserved as a row of approximately 30 feathers of a consistent small size that attach perpendicularly to the ulna and third metacarpal of the specimen.

facts.statement: The right wing shows approximately 10 primary feathers and 20 secondary feathers, with primaries being longer.
facts.quote: The specimen's better-preserved right wing shows that the primary feathers were longer than its secondaries, and the authors estimate approximately 10 primaries and 20 secondaries.

facts.statement: Long vaned feathers ran along the tail, preserved as projections at a 45-degree angle from the vertebrae.
facts.quote: Long vaned feathers were also present along the length of the tail, and are preserved as a series of long projections of vanes at a 45-degree angle from the tail vertebrae.

facts.statement: The presence of large wings on a non-flying dromaeosaur raises questions about their function.
facts.quote: raising the question of what function such wings would serve.

facts.statement: It is impossible to determine if Zhenyuanlong's body feathers were simple filaments or complex structures with a central vane.
facts.quote: Whether the animal's body feathers were simple and non-shafted or more complex filaments attaching to a central vane is impossible to determine from this specimen.

facts.statement: Due to preservation issues, the symmetry of the tail feathers cannot be fully assessed, though they resemble those of other bird-like dinosaurs.
facts.quote: While preservation makes symmetry difficult to assess, these feathers appear generally similar to the tail feathers of other birdlike dinosaurs that preserve this region, including Sinornithosaurus, Jinfengopteryx, Anchiornis, Eosinopteryx, and Archaeopteryx.

facts.statement: Because the tail tip is missing, it cannot be ruled out that Zhenyuanlong had a fan-like structure at the end of its tail.
facts.quote: However, since the end of Zhenyuanlongs tail is not preserved, it's impossible to rule out the presence of a fan entirely.

facts.statement: Zhenyuanlong lived during the Early Cretaceous, approximately 125 million years ago in the Aptian stage, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a principios del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 125 millones de años, en el Aptiense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen JPM-0008, an almost complete skeleton with skull and jaws, was found in the Yixian Formation in Liaoning Province, China.
facts.quote: El holotipo, JPM-0008, un esqueleto casi completo con cráneo y mandíbulas, fue encontrado en la Formación Yixian, en la provincia de Liaoning, en China.

facts.statement: Zhenyuanlong was covered in feathers over its entire body, including large wings and long tail feathers.
facts.quote: Presenta plumas por todo su cuerpo, además de grandes alas y largas plumas en la cola.

facts.statement: Including the tail feathers, Zhenyuanlong could have reached a total length of 2 meters in life.
facts.quote: Con la añadida longitud de las plumas de la cola, el animal pudo haber tenido 2 metros de longitud fácilmente en vida.

facts.statement: Zhenyuanlong had very short arms and the shortest arm-to-leg length ratio of all known dromaeosaurids, except for the basal Mahakala and the giant unenlagiine Austroraptor.
facts.quote: Zhenyuanlong tenía brazos muy cortos y la proporción de longitud de brazo a pierna más corta de todos los dromeosáuridos conocidos, excepto el dromeosáurido basal Mahakala y el gigante unenlagiínido Austroraptor.

facts.statement: Despite having modern-looking wings, Zhenyuanlong was likely too large and heavy to fly or glide.
facts.quote: Despite the modern-looking wings, due to this size and weight the animal was unlikely to be able to "fly or glide or do anything in the air".

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the most viable function for Zhenyuanlong's wings was sexual display, such as threatening rivals or courting mates, similar to how a peacock uses its tail.
facts.quote: According to the authors and other paleontologists, the most viable hypothesis at this time is the use of the wings in sexual display, either to threaten rivals or to court potential mates, much as a peacock uses its tail to impress hens.

facts.statement: Alternative hypotheses for Zhenyuanlong's wings include protecting eggs in the nest or some form of arboreal gliding.
facts.quote: Other possibilities include the use of wings in displaying to mates or rivals, protecting eggs in its nest, or even some amount of arboreal gliding.

facts.quote: El fósil representa a un individuo subadulto, como lo muestra la fusión de los arcos neurales.habiendo sido progresado hacia el sacro.

facts.statement: Zhenyuanlong is unique among Liaoning dromaeosaurids because its second metacarpal is shorter than the combined lengths of the first metacarpal and the first bone of the innermost digit.
facts.quote: Zhenyuanlong también es único entre los dromeosáuridos de Liaoning porque su segundo metacarpiano es más corto que las longitudes combinadas del primer metacarpiano y el primer hueso del dedo más interno.

facts.statement: Zhenyuanlong had a furry coat of simple filaments over most of its body and large feathered wings and tail.
facts.quote: El fósil tipo de Zhenyuanlong conserva el tegumento en varias partes del espécimen, incluida una capa "peluda" de filamentos simples sobre la mayor parte del cuerpo y plumas grandes y con paletas en la cola y los brazos

facts.statement: Body feathers were preserved only as small impressions on the front and back of the neck.

facts.statement: Despite having small arms, Zhenyuanlong's wing feathers were very long, more than twice the length of the upper arm bone.
facts.quote: A pesar de sus pequeños brazos, las plumas que componían las alas eran muy largas, más del doble de la longitud del húmero

facts.statement: The right wing showed a complex overlapping arrangement of primary feathers on the second finger, secondary feathers on the forearm, and coverts covering both sets.
facts.quote: El ala derecha del espécimen muestra un complejo superpuesto de plumas primarias, que se adhieren al segundo dedo de la mano, plumas secundarias, que se adhieren al antebrazo y coberteras, que cubren ambos conjuntos

facts.statement: Long feathered tail plumes were preserved as a series of projections at a 45-degree angle from the tail vertebrae.

facts.statement: Unlike some close relatives, the Zhenyuanlong specimen preserves no feathers on its hind limbs.

facts.statement: Zhenyuanlong was about 2 meters long and covered in complex feathers, making it virtually indistinguishable from a large bird in life.
